identity.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia (Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes)
native_names: Краљевина Срба, Хрвата и Словенаца (Kraljevina Srba, Hrvata i Slovenaca)
alt_names: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes

land.text: Serbia in its 1913 borders with Vojvodina and Montenegro

predecessors.note: The Kingdom of Serbia (Cliopatria 'Serbs'): it absorbed Syrmia, Banat, Backa and Baranja on 24-25 November 1918, Montenegro on 28 November 1918, and united with the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs on 1 December 1918 (serbs ledger 28-31). The Kingdom page: 'Established: 1 December 1918' and 'Montenegro having been absorbed into Serbia the previous month'. The 'serbia' dossier below is the Macedonian-front remnant row, which review eu-21-a failed as a duplicate of serbs; drop that entry if the dossier is removed.

land.text: the Kingdom of Serbia, which united with the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs on 1 December 1918

predecessors.note: The Kingdom page gives 'Established: 1 December 1918' and says Montenegro had been 'absorbed into Serbia the previous month'; the union itself is described in the serbia dossier.

land.text: Montenegro, 'absorbed into Serbia the previous month' (November 1918)

predecessors.note: A Cliopatria row 'Montenegro' runs 1853-2024, so the interwar years are inside that row too. Montenegro merged into Serbia in November 1918 (montenegro ledger 13, serbs ledger 30), so it comes to this state through the serbs predecessor.

land.text: the South Slav lands of Austria-Hungary

predecessors.note: No dossier yet (named as a successor in the austria-hungary dossier); no page opened here describes the union.

land.text: the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia, proclaimed 29 November 1945

successors.note: Cliopatria row 'Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia' (1946-1991) shares Wikidata Q83286; it is a different state (monarchy abolished on 29 November 1945), so it keeps its own dossier.

capitals.name: Belgrade
capitals.note: 'Capital and largest city: Belgrade' (infobox). [Fix pass: the London seat of the government-in-exile is not a capital because it lies outside every shape of the state: the Kingdom page lists 'Government-in-exile: April 1941' and 'A royal government-in-exile ... was established in London', the king being in exile from 13/14 April 1941; no capital is drawn from 1941 to the liberation of Belgrade on 20 October 1944 (next entry).]

capitals.name: Belgrade
capitals.note: The second Tito-Subasic agreement was signed 'in the recently liberated Yugoslav capital of Belgrade' on 1 November 1944; the infobox of Democratic Federal Yugoslavia gives Belgrade.

rulers.name: Peter I
rulers.note: 1 December 1918 - 16 August 1921; 'Prince regent Alexander ruled in the name of the King'.

rulers.name: Peter II
rulers.note: 9 October 1934 - 29 November 1945, 'in exile from 13/14 April 1941'; deposed by the Constituent Assembly on 29 November 1945.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row starts in 1919 but the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes was established on 1 December 1918. The 1919 shape is used for the last month of 1918; unverified beyond the establishment date (page budget).

244,290 km2 against the infobox's 247,542 km2 (1941): ratio 0.99. The Kingdom page names Vojvodina ('Banat, Backa and Baranja') as ceded by Trianon and the shape already contains it. The 1,907 km2 added in the 1920 shape fits the 2,563 km2 Bulgaria ceded at Neuilly (27 November 1919).

correction.text: the 1920 shape without Zadar, the Italian Province of Zara (the small islands are below the shape's resolution)

keyframe_review.note: 246,197 km2, ratio 0.99 to the infobox 247,542 km2. The shape still contains the Zadar area (7 cells within 40 km of Zadar), which Rapallo (12 November 1920) gave to Italy: 'the city of Zadar (as the Province of Zara)', with the islands of Cres, Losinj, Lastovo and Palagruza. The rest of what Rapallo gave Italy (Istria, Trieste, Gorizia) was Habsburg land that the shape never contained.

246,055 km2, ratio 0.99 to the infobox 247,542 km2 (1941, the first area the page gives). The Kingdom page: he changed the internal divisions 'to nine new banovinas on 3 October' 1929, and 'on 26 August 1939, Vladko Macek became vice premier' (the infobox says the Sporazum was 25 August 1939): internal autonomy, no border change. The shape holds to 1940.

union.text: Backa, Baranja, Medjimurje and the north-eastern Prekmurje
the Independent State of Croatia proclaimed on 10 April 1941
the southern part of Slovenia as the Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia and the Bay of Kotor
Serbia, under direct German military administration

correction.text: Yugoslavia within the 1940 lines minus the lands annexed by Hungary, the Independent State of Croatia, Italy and Albania (Kosovo), and minus Serbia and Montenegro, which are the Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia and the Italian governorate; Vardar Macedonia and northern Slovenia stay as occupied land

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1941-1944, which Cliopatria lacks (its next shape is 1945). The state continued in exile in London and its land was partitioned on 6-17 April 1941: Hungary annexed the north-east, the Independent State of Croatia (10 April) took Croatia and Bosnia, Italy annexed the Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia and the Bay of Kotor (and Kosovo, which went to Italian Albania), Bulgaria took Macedonia on 19 April. Serbia (German military administration) and Montenegro (Italian governorate) have their own dossiers; what stays on the map as Yugoslav land is Vardar Macedonia (Bulgarian occupation) and northern Slovenia (German occupation), hatched as occupied. [Fix pass: the government-in-exile sat in London from April 1941; London is not a capital of this dossier because it lies outside every shape, and the land retaken by the Partisans in 1944 is booked in the yugoslav-partisans dossier and carried here by the March 1945 merge.]

250,300 km2 against the infobox 255,804 km2 for Democratic Federal Yugoslavia: ratio 0.98. The shape holds about 2,800 km2 of Istria (the Rijeka area). The page does not describe Istria, Rijeka, Zadar, the Julian March or Trieste in 1945; unverified: page budget. [Fix pass: the Julian March page says 'In May 1945, the Yugoslav Army entered Trieste' and 'Zone B was under Yugoslav administration' (Morgan Line, June 1945). The 21 cells of this shape that the 1936 shape lacks (18 in Istria and the Slovene Littoral, about 4,500 km2) are land the Yugoslav army occupied while Italy kept the sovereignty until the 1947 treaties; the ledger carries them as an occupation pair (May-November 1945).]

region.text: the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes: Serbia, Montenegro and the former Habsburg South Slav lands

ledger.note: 1 December 1918: the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes is established. 'Established: 1 December 1918'; 'From 1918 to 1929, it was officially called the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes.' [Fix pass after review eu-21-b: the Kingdom page (re-read 2026-11-01) says Montenegro had been 'absorbed into Serbia the previous month', so Montenegro enters the Kingdom through the Kingdom of Serbia (serbs ledger 30, 28 November 1918; montenegro ledger 13), not as a gain of this state; the earlier gain of 'Montenegro in November 1918' predated the state and is deleted. The region of this event, the 1919 shape, already holds it. The found counterpart is now serbs, the Kingdom of Serbia dossier that dissolves on 1 December 1918.]

region.text: south-eastern Carinthia, inhabited partly by Slovenians, the plebiscite area

ledger.note: 1919: the dispute over south-eastern Carinthia begins. The First Austrian Republic page says only that the south-east 'was inhabited partly by Slovenians' and gives the plebiscite of 1920; the start of the dispute is a bridge over a silence (the same bridge as republic-of-austria ledger 1). Added after review eu-21-b.

region.text: a portion of the Alpine provinces (Lower Styria around Maribor is the researcher's reading; the page does not name it)

ledger.note: 10 September 1919: the Treaty of Saint-Germain gives 'a portion of the Alpine provinces to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes' (First Austrian Republic page, the same page as the republic-of-austria loss). The page does not name Lower Styria or Maribor; the land is the researcher's reading. Mirror of republic-of-austria ledger 3, added after review eu-21-b.

region.text: 2,563 km2 on the western border, the Pirot and Pcinja districts including Dimitrovgrad and Bosilegrad, and part of North Macedonia

ledger.note: 27 November 1919: the Treaty of Neuilly gives the kingdom a strip of Bulgaria. The treaty required Bulgaria 'to cede a further area of 2,563 km2 on its western border' (1,545 km2 in present-day Serbia and 1,028 km2 in North Macedonia).

region.text: Croatia-Slavonia, Medjimurje, Banat, Backa and Baranja, and two-thirds of the Slovene March (Prekmurje)

ledger.note: 4 June 1920: Trianon confirms the north and east. The Kingdom page: 'Vojvodina was ceded to Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes'; the Trianon page: 'Croatia-Slavonia, Medjimurje, Banat, Backa and Baranja, and two-thirds of the Slovene March (Prekmurje)'; Pecs, Mohacs, Baja and Szigetvar stayed Hungarian. The shape of 1919 already contained Vojvodina. The Romanian share of Banat is not part of this.

region.text: south-eastern Carinthia, inhabited partly by Slovenians, the plebiscite area

ledger.note: 10 October 1920: the Carinthian plebiscite keeps the south-east in Austria. 'a Carinthian plebiscite on October 10, 1920, and the majority chose to remain with Austria' (First Austrian Republic page); the Kingdom page: Carinthia 'opted to remain in Austria'. No land changes hands. Added after review eu-21-b.

region.text: the city of Zadar (as the Province of Zara) and a few of the Dalmatian islands

ledger.note: 12 November 1920: the Treaty of Rapallo gives Italy Zadar and islands. 'The treaty, signed on 12 November 1920 in Rapallo': Article 2 gave Italy 'the city of Zadar (as the Province of Zara)'; Article 3 the islands Cres, Losinj, Lastovo and Palagruza; Article 4 set up the Free State of Fiume (Rijeka), Susak stayed with the kingdom. Istria, Trieste and Gorizia (Article 1) were Habsburg land the kingdom never held.

3 October 1929: the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes becomes the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. 'He changed the official name of the country to Kingdom of Yugoslavia on 3 October 1929' and replaced the 33 oblasts by nine banovinas.

region.text: Montenegro

ledger.note: 1941: Montenegro passes to Italy. Italy 'gained control over Montenegro' (the Italian governorate has its own dossier, found 18 April 1941); the page gives no month, and after the armistice of 8 September 1943 'The former Italian kingdoms of Albania and of Montenegro were placed under German occupation'.

region.text: the southern part of Slovenia as the Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia and the Bay of Kotor

ledger.note: 1941: Italy annexes land on the Adriatic. Italy 'annexed the southern part as the Ljubljana Province' (of Slovenia) and 'large sections of Dalmatia' and 'the Bay of Kotor'. The page does not date the annexations; Dalmatia is approximated by the whole region.

region.text: Kosovo

ledger.note: 1941: Kosovo passes to Italian-ruled Albania. The page says Italy 'also annexed Kosovo' (it does not name Albania); the Albanian dossier records Kosovo joining Albania in spring 1941.

region.text: Backa, Baranja, Medjimurje and the north-eastern Prekmurje

ledger.note: April 1941: Hungary occupies and annexes the north-east. The Hungarian occupation page: 'The occupation began on 11 April 1941 when 80,000 Hungarian troops crossed the Yugoslav border'; 'Annexed by Hungary: 14 December 1941' (Backa, Baranja, Medjimurje, Prekmurje). The Axis occupation page: Hungary 'occupied and subsequently annexed Vojvodina, Baranja, Backa and Medjimurje' and 'the northeastern Prekmurje region'. The loss is dated to the occupation (April), as in the hungarian-republic gain; the formal incorporation was 14 December.

region.text: the whole kingdom

ledger.note: 6 April 1941: the Axis invades Yugoslavia. The war 'began on 6 April 1941, when the country was invaded and swiftly conquered by Axis forces' (Germany, Italy, Hungary and Bulgaria).

region.text: the Independent State of Croatia proclaimed on 10 April 1941

ledger.note: 10 April 1941: the Independent State of Croatia is proclaimed. Slavko Kvaternik 'proclaimed the Independent State of Croatia (NDH)' on behalf of the Ustase, with German assistance; the page gives no boundaries, so the region is Cliopatria's Croatian shape.

region.text: the whole kingdom

ledger.note: 17 April 1941: Yugoslavia capitulates. The war ended with 'the unconditional surrender signed by General Danilo Kalafatovic on 17 April'. The king left for exile on 13/14 April 1941 and a royal government-in-exile was established in London ('in exile from 13/14 April 1941'); the seat is not a capital in this dossier (London lies outside every shape), so the earlier capital_move event is folded into this note after review eu-21-b.

region.text: nearly all of modern North Macedonia and parts of eastern Serbia

ledger.note: 19 April 1941: Bulgaria enters Macedonia and eastern Serbia. The Bulgarian army 'moved into nearly all of modern North Macedonia and parts of eastern Serbia on 19 April 1941' and formally annexed them with Greek Thrace 'on 14 May'; the Bulgarian dossier models the zone as an occupation to 1944.

region.text: 'most of modern central Serbia, along with the northern part of Kosovo and the Banat' (the page's words, 'the northern part of Kosovo (around Kosovska Mitrovica)'): Serbia without Bačka (Hungarian), Syrmia (Croatian, though 'an area of eastern Syrmia was initially included') and the Pirot district (Bulgarian), plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities

ledger.note: April 1941: Serbia passes to German military rule. Germany 'placed it under direct military administration'; a Nedic-led government took over from 29 August 1941. The Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia has its own dossier (found 22 April 1941); this page gives no day. [Fix pass: the region was the whole modern Republic of Serbia, which overlapped the Backa loss to Hungary, Srem in the Independent State of Croatia and the Pirot occupation; it is now the found region of the Territory dossier (Serbia without Backa, Srem and the Pirot district, plus the four northern Kosovo municipalities). Those four municipalities also lie inside the Kosovo loss to Albania above, a small overlap kept because the Territory dossier holds them.]

region.text: the largest, northern part of Slovenia

ledger.note: April 1941: Germany takes northern Slovenia. Germany 'occupied the largest, northern part of Slovenia' (the German dossier records an annexation on its own page).

29 November 1943: the Partisans' AVNOJ creates Democratic Federal Yugoslavia. The new state arose 'de facto on 29 November 1943 through the Second Session of the Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia'; the name was 'officially adopted on 17 February 1944'. The kingdom's exile government and the Partisans reached the Tito-Subasic agreement on 16 June 1944.

region.text: nearly all of modern North Macedonia and parts of eastern Serbia

ledger.note: 1944: Bulgaria leaves Macedonia and eastern Serbia. 'Bulgarian armies entered Yugoslavia at dawn on 8 October 1944' as Soviet allies; the Democratic Federal Yugoslavia page gives Vardar Macedonia as 'Annexed by the Kingdom of Bulgaria (1941-1944)'.
20 October 1944: Belgrade is liberated and again the seat. 'The Red Army took the city on 20 October'; the second Tito-Subasic agreement was signed there on 1 November 1944.

region.text: the Independent State of Croatia proclaimed on 10 April 1941

ledger.note: 1945: the Independent State of Croatia is overrun. The Partisans 'launched a general offensive in the Mostar-Visegrad-Drina sector' on 20 March 1945; Germany left Mostar on 12 February and Sarajevo on 15 April 1945. The Croatian dossier dissolves the state on 8 May 1945; this page gives no date for Zagreb.

region.text: the largest, northern part of Slovenia

ledger.note: 1945: the German occupation of northern Slovenia ends. Page silent on Slovenia; the German dossier gives May 1945 (bridging a silence). [Fix pass: pages tried for the date in the fix pass and silent: Yugoslav Front, Axis occupation of Yugoslavia, Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral (its units surrendered to the New Zealand 2nd Division 'on the evening of 2 May', which concerns Trieste, not northern Slovenia) and Julian March; confidence stays 1. The nazi-germany dossier (ledger 67, January 1945) ends the occupation of Serbia, not of northern Slovenia, and has no record of the Slovene occupation.]

region.text: the Ljubljana Province and the Bay of Kotor, the Italian-annexed lands that Germany took after the armistice of 8 September 1943

ledger.note: 1945: the Ljubljana Province and the Bay of Kotor return from German hands; the Italian-annexed lands had passed from Italy to Germany in September 1943 (kingdom-of-italy ledger 38, confidence 1). The Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral page: it was 'established, with its headquarters in Trieste, on 10 September 1943' after the Italian capitulation and 'comprised the provinces of Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pula (Pola), Rijeka (Fiume) and Ljubljana (Lubiana)'. The Axis occupation page puts the former Italian Montenegro under German occupation and says the Governorship of Dalmatia's possessions were divided between Germany and the Independent State of Croatia (Sidraga-Ravni Kotari); it does not name the Bay of Kotor. No page opened (Yugoslav Front, Axis occupation, Operational Zone, Julian March) dates the return: the year 1945 is a bridge, confidence 1. [Fix pass after review eu-21-b: the counterpart was kingdom-of-italy, which had lost the land in 1943, and Dalmatia was in the region. Dalmatia is dropped here: the Partisan-held coast is carried by the March 1945 merge and the part the Independent State of Croatia held comes back in the 1945 gain from that state.]

region.text: Medjimurje and Prekmurje, annexed by Hungary in 1941

ledger.note: 1945: Medjimurje and Prekmurje return. The Hungarian occupation page: 'Medjimurje and Prekmurje remained occupied until the last weeks of the war'; no exact date. Backa and Baranja came back to the Partisans in October 1944 and are carried by the March 1945 merge.

region.text: the land the Partisans held in March 1945: their 1944 shape plus the land booked as Partisan gains in 1944 (Montenegro, Belgrade and Serbia without Srem, Vardar Macedonia, the Dalmatian coast) and Kosovo; the Syrmian front still held in the west

ledger.note: March 1945: the Partisan movement and the exile government form one government. 'Provisional government formed: 7 March 1945' (the Axis page says 8 March: 'a coalition Yugoslav government was formed in Belgrade with Tito as Premier'). [Fix pass after review eu-21-b: this merge now carries the land the Partisans, not the exile government, retook in 1944. The three 1944 gains booked to this Kingdom (Backa from Hungary, Montenegro from the Italian governorate, Serbia from the Territory of the Military Commander) are deleted because the counterpart dossiers give that land to the Partisans (yugoslav-partisans ledger 7, 9, 10; territory-of-the-military-commander-in-serbia ledger 5; hungarian-republic loss of October 1944); the 1945 gain of Kosovo from albania is deleted for the same reason (albania ledger 20: 1944 loss to the Partisans, confidence 1; no page opened dates the Partisan entry into Kosovo). The date of the merge is the page's, the region is the researcher's reading, hence confidence 2. The yugoslav-partisans dossier names no counterpart for its dissolution (it should name yugoslavia).]

region.text: the Julian March east of the Morgan Line (Zone B and the Slovene Littoral, Istria and the Fiume coast); the provinces are the researcher's reading, as in the socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia dossier

ledger.note: May 1945: the Yugoslav army occupies the Julian March. The Julian March page: 'In May 1945, the Yugoslav Army entered Trieste'; 'The Morgan Line was drawn in June 1945, dividing the region into two militarily administered zones'; 'Zone B was under Yugoslav administration'. Italy kept the sovereignty until the 1947 treaties, so this is occupied, not annexed, land; it explains the 21 cells of the 1945 shape that the 1936 shape lacks (18 in Istria and the Slovene Littoral). The socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia dossier opens the same occupation in November 1945 and continues it. Added after review eu-21-b.

region.text: the Julian March east of the Morgan Line (Zone B and the Slovene Littoral, Istria and the Fiume coast); the provinces are the researcher's reading, as in the socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia dossier

ledger.note: 29 November 1945: the monarchy is abolished and the occupation passes to the Federal People's Republic (socialist-federal-republic-of-yugoslavia ledger 1), so this end only closes the pair for this dossier; the occupation itself lasts until the 1947 peace treaty took effect.

region.text: the whole state at the end of 1945

ledger.note: 29 November 1945: the monarchy is abolished and the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia is proclaimed. 'On 29 November, King Peter II was deposed (and the monarchy abolished) by Yugoslavia's Communist Constituent Assembly while he was still in exile'; 'the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia was proclaimed on 29 November 1945' (Democratic Federal Yugoslavia page).

wars.name: Invasion of Yugoslavia
wars.outcome: Yugoslavia invaded on 6 April 1941 and capitulated on 17 April; the Independent State of Croatia was proclaimed on 10 April, Hungary, Italy and Bulgaria annexed or occupied the periphery and Germany occupied Serbia and northern Slovenia; the king left for London.
wars.note: The Kingdom page gives the same two dates.

the Independent State of Croatia proclaimed on 10 April 1941
the southern part of Slovenia as the Ljubljana Province, large sections of Dalmatia and the Bay of Kotor
Serbia, under direct German military administration

zones.text: Yugoslavia within the 1940 lines minus the lands annexed by Hungary, the Independent State of Croatia, Italy and Albania (Kosovo), and minus Serbia and Montenegro, which are the Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia and the Italian governorate; Vardar Macedonia and northern Slovenia stay as occupied land

wars.outcome: The Partisans controlled the eastern half of the country by late 1944; the Red Army took Belgrade on 20 October 1944; the German withdrawal from Sarajevo on 15 April 1945; a coalition government on 7-8 March 1945; the monarchy abolished on 29 November 1945.
wars.note: The Partisans have their own rebel dossier (yugoslav-partisans, 1941-1945).

certainty.note: The kingdom was established on 1 December 1918 with unsettled frontiers in Carinthia, Banat and the Adriatic.
Trianon (1920), Neuilly (1919) and Rapallo (12 November 1920) fixed the frontiers; the Carinthian plebiscite of 1920 left the south-east of Carinthia in Austria.
Annexation and occupation lines of the Axis partition are not on the pages opened.
Istria, Rijeka, Zadar and the Julian March were still undecided until the 1947 Paris treaty.

notes:
Cliopatria 'Yugoslavia' (1919-1945, Q83286) and 'Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia' (1946-1991) share a Wikidata id but are different states: the Kingdom was abolished on 29 November 1945 and the republic proclaimed the same day; the SFRY dossier already starts in November 1945 and names this one as predecessor, so no merge. The 1941-1944 gap in Cliopatria is filled by a new 1941 keyframe (the occupied rump) plus the ledger's annexations and occupations; the 1945 shape is accepted as it stands. The Partisans (yugoslav-partisans, a rebel dossier by another batch) are recorded as a merge in March 1945; the contest between the exile government, the Chetniks and the Partisans is not on the pages opened. Counterparts still without a dossier: state-of-slovenes-croats-and-serbs (October-December 1918) and the Italian governorates of Dalmatia and the Ljubljana Province; the Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia and the Italian governorate of Montenegro (eu-21-x) are used as counterparts for Serbia and Montenegro 1941-1944. Pages silent: the Hungarian entry into Backa, the Italian annexation dates, the German annexation of northern Slovenia (the Axis occupation page says 'occupied'; the German dossier says annexed on its own page), Istria, Rijeka, Zadar and the Julian March in 1945, Carinthia (the Kingdom page: it 'opted to remain in Austria' without a date). The Kingdom page and the Democratic Federal Yugoslavia page disagree on the day of the Croat agreement (25 versus 26 August 1939) and the provisional government (7 versus 8 March 1945). Gazetteer names used that may be missing: 'North Macedonia' and 'Kosovo' as countries exist; none else. Six pages are cited (five budget plus Trianon, already open for the Hungarian dossier).

Fix pass after review eu-21-b (2026-11-01). Applied: (1) the November 1918 gain of Montenegro is deleted (Kingdom page: 'Montenegro having been absorbed into Serbia the previous month'; serbs ledger 30 and montenegro ledger 13 carry it); serbs is the first predecessor and the found counterpart. (2) The 1944 gains of Backa, Montenegro and Serbia and the 1945 gain of Kosovo are deleted: the counterpart dossiers give that land to the Partisans, and the March 1945 merge (region widened to the Partisan-held land, confidence 2) carries it. The hungarian-republic loss of Backa and Baranja now names yugoslav-partisans (October 1944) and the loss of Medjimurje and Prekmurje names yugoslavia (1945, mirrored here). (3) The 1945 return of the Italian-annexed lands names nazi-germany, not kingdom-of-italy, and covers the Ljubljana Province and the Bay of Kotor; Dalmatia is dropped (Partisan coast in the merge, NDH part in the NDH gain). (4) The Serbian loss uses the Territory dossier's region. (5) Lower Styria (gain, 10 September 1919) and the Carinthian contest (1919 - 10 October 1920) mirror republic-of-austria, from the First Austrian Republic page; the Kingdom page says Carinthia 'opted to remain in Austria'. (6) London is no longer a capital and the capital_move to London is folded into the April 1941 note. (7) The Julian March occupation by the Yugoslav army (May-November 1945) explains the 1945 shape's extra cells. (8) The month of the Backa loss is April 1941 (Hungarian occupation page: 11 April; annexation 14 December). Not settled: the dates of the end of the German occupation of northern Slovenia and of the return of the Ljubljana Province, the Bay of Kotor and Kosovo (no page opened gives them; all stay at confidence 1). Disagreements: none with the reviewer; the 'serbia' dossier is kept as a second predecessor for the Cliopatria 'Serbia' 1918 row and should be dropped if the orchestrator removes it. Routing: yugoslav-partisans lacks Backa and Baranja (October 1944), Kosovo and a counterpart yugoslavia on its dissolve; nazi-germany lacks the occupation of northern Slovenia and ends its occupation of Hungary in May 1945 against 4 April on the Hungarian page; kingdom-of-italy books South Tyrol from austria-hungary.
